member.name: T:Maths.Rng.Xoshiro256PlusPlus
member.summary: xoshiro256++ pseudo-random generator (Blackman & Vigna 2018) with raw 4-word state save/restore. .NET 6+'s unseeded and use a xoshiro256 family generator internally, but do not expose its state — this class exists so SPC checkpoint artifacts can roundtrip RNG state bit-identically across save/restore boundaries.

remarks.para: Variant. This is xoshiro256++ — the scrambler is rotl(s0 + s3, 23) + s0. Equivalent statistical quality to xoshiro256** but a different output function; the two are not interchangeable. The state-advance is identical across both variants.

Seeding. An seed is expanded to four state words via SplitMix64 (Vigna's recommended xoshiro initializer). A seed draws 32 bytes from for OS-entropy bootstrapping. The all-zero state is a fixed point of the recurrence and is guarded against in both seeding paths.

Provisional placement. Lives under Clustering.Graphical.SPC.Potts for now to keep the SPC spine compiling, but xoshiro is a generic numerics primitive — should migrate to src/numerics (or wherever shared numerical primitives land) when that namespace is established.

member.name: M:Maths.Rng.Xoshiro256PlusPlus.NextDouble
member.summary: Uniform in [0, 1). Uses the top 53 bits of one generator output — the canonical conversion for IEEE-754 double precision.

member.name: M:Maths.Rng.Xoshiro256PlusPlus.NextInt(System.Int32)
member.summary: Uniform in [0, q). Multiplication-shift on the upper 32 bits of a state output — bias is q / 2^32, negligible for Potts-scale q (≤ ~30).

member.summary: SplitMix64 step — Vigna's recommended xoshiro seed initializer. Each call advances by the golden-ratio constant and returns a well-distributed 64-bit word.
